text:
Not guilty, but only if the arrest lacked probable cause (the facts say only that the officer "believed" the suspect was involved) and the jury believes the suspect's account, that the nightstick blows began after he cursed and his punch was meant to stop them. Under the officer's account, the punch was resistance to an arrest and the suspect would be guilty of assault. My earlier answer did not address the arrest's lawfulness, which the team note indicates is decisive.

CONFIDENCE: 45
